rows.do_not_add_to: Do not add to, average with, or substitute for WHO regional figures (WHO 2024 report Fig. 2, p. 14); do not sum with the article's other regional figures, which together exceed its own global total; do not cite as a WHO or GHE 2021 figure.
rows.note: Cites the WHO 2024 report, which prints 15 000 deaths and 1.7 per 100 000 for the European Region in 2021 (p. 14, Fig. 2); 9,155 and 1.0 appear nowhere in that report. The article's global total 295,210 equals the GBD 2017 estimate for 2017 (Franklin et al., Inj Prev 2020), and its Africa 77,000, Eastern Mediterranean 36,000 and Americas 16,500 also differ from the report's 66 000, 35 000 and 17 000. Primary origin of 9,155 not found; year and cause definition unverified. Reviewer may prefer to drop this row.

notes: Findings. (1) WHO Global status report on drowning prevention 2024 (ISBN 978-92-4-010396-2; read via the Spanish health-ministry mirror because iris.who.int refused the fetch) prints for the WHO European Region in 2021: 15 000 deaths (5% of global) and 1.7 per 100 000 (p. 14 text and Fig. 2 'Number and rate of drowning deaths by WHO region'). Data source: WHO Global Health Estimates 2021 (p. 12). Definition: ICD-10 W65-W74 unintentional drowning (p. 8); Box 3 (p. 8) lists exclusions X71, X92, Y21, V90, V92, X38; migrant drownings excluded (WHO news release 13 Dec 2024, note to editors). Region = 53 Member States (WHO Europe statement 24 Jul 2023). (2) The 9,155 / 1.0 pair was found only in a secondary article on esanum.com ('Drowning: an underestimated global emergency', undated; image path 2025/8/21), which cites the WHO 2024 report but prints figures the report does not contain: global 295,210; Africa 77,000 (5.7 per 100,000); Eastern Mediterranean 36,000; Americas 16,500; Western Pacific and South-East Asia about 83,000 each; Europe 9,155 (1.0). Its global 295,210 is exactly the GBD 2017 global estimate for 2017 (Franklin et al., Inj Prev 2020;26:i83-i95). Its regional values summed (about 304,700) exceed its own global total, so the set is internally inconsistent. (3) I could not confirm a primary source for 9,155: it is not in the WHO report text I could read (pp. 1-46; the mirror's extracted text ends there, so annexes and country profiles were not checked), not in Franklin et al.'s main text (regional values sit in supplementary table S1, which was unreachable), and GBD 2021 gives 274,200 global deaths in 2021, so 295,210 is not GBD 2021 either. The rate 1.0 per 100,000 with 9,155 deaths implies about 915 million people, consistent with the whole WHO European Region, not the EU (Eurostat EU-27 2021: 5 004). (4) Reconciliation: the two figures are not two valid measurements of the same quantity. 15 000 / 1.7 is the WHO primary figure (WHO European Region, 2021, GHE 2021, W65-W74). 9,155 / 1.0 has no identifiable primary source and is most likely a GBD 2017-based estimate for 2017 (unconfirmed), mislabelled as 2021 and misattributed to WHO. Recommendation: keep who-region-eur at 15 000 / 1.7 with the scope note proposed in corrections; do not record 9,155 as a WHO figure. I added it only as a grade-C row with a do-not-add rule so the discrepancy stays documented; the reviewer may prefer to drop that row. (5) Other European figures seen, different scopes, not reconciled: WHO Europe statement 24 Jul 2023 'estimated 20 000 people each year' (scope and year undefined); Eurostat EU-27 deaths by drowning and submersion 5 004 (2021) and 4 810 (2022), dataset hlth_cd_aro; ILS Europe 2020 post 'about 35.000 victims in the European Region' (unsourced). None equals 9,155. (6) Corrections carry old = 'not read' because the ledger could not be opened in this run (no repository access); the reviewer should fill in the current values. Blocked fetches (permission not granted in time): ghoapi.azureedge.net indicator list; OWID CSV; cdn.who.int GHE xlsx; pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov (PMC7571364, PMC11961984). All quotes are 25 words or fewer and taken from fetched pages only.
